gfi_title: Targeted alternative protein industry events & workshops
scope_note: Convening for human-food protein; context for T1 and P1
vietnam_angle: Weak. We found no alternative-protein event held in Vietnam in 2025 to 2026. The main ingredient fair, Fi Vietnam (Ho Chi Minh City, biennial, 300+ exhibitors expected), lists no plant-protein or fermentation theme. Vietnam took part in a 2021 WHO Western Pacific and GFI regulatory workshop
vietnam_evidence: Searches in English and Vietnamese found no event; Fi Vietnam page lists sectors without protein (SLW-11); 2021 WHO WPRO workshop attendees included Vietnam (SLW-12); Humane World chef training in 2025 already in the package (AFN-23)
verdict_note: An event is a tool, not a solution. The study's plays need specific meetings (T1 buyers and extrusion suppliers; P1 regulators), and these can use existing venues such as Fi Vietnam 2028 or a ministry workshop when a play needs one. No separate events programme is justified
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese buyer or regulator asks for a technical session on textured protein or new-food rules; a protein theme at Fi Vietnam 2028

vietnam_angle: Moderate. GFI's database (titled 2021) shows no Vietnamese funder or eligibility. NAFOSTED is the main domestic channel and runs joint calls with FWO, DFG, SNSF and UK bodies. No GFI-funded work in OpenAlex has a Vietnamese affiliation (0 of 270)
vietnam_evidence: NAFOSTED 2023: 284 projects, VND 278.3 billion approved; ordinary basic-research project about VND 950 million, strong-group project about VND 3 billion (SLW-01). On 525 Vietnam-affiliated food-protein works, NAFOSTED is acknowledged on 36 and VINIF on 5 (SLW-02). GFI grants closed on 15 October 2026 (RD-02)
verdict_note: Adds grant sizes and partner calls to ch06 6.6 and research_funding.csv, closes OQ-387 and partly OQ-054 and OQ-126, and gives RM-11 a scale check: USD 5 to 15 million a year is about 47% to 140% of all NAFOSTED approvals in 2023 (our calculation). A separate Vietnamese funding database is not needed: research_funding.csv already does this job
signal_to_watch: A NAFOSTED thematic or directed call naming food protein; a GFI or other alternative-protein call open to Vietnamese applicants; a first Vietnamese GFI grantee

gfi_title: Build alternative protein sessions into scientific conferences
vietnam_angle: Weak. Vietnamese food-protein research is thin (69 Vietnam-affiliated records on alternative-protein terms since 2018, at most 6 at any one institution) and much of it is not indexed abroad
vietnam_evidence: OpenAlex count and institution spread (SLW-02); ch06 6.1 and 6.7 already advise publishing in indexed journals (BIB-01)
verdict_note: Research groups can propose sessions at will at no public cost. It does not need a programme, and there is too little Vietnamese work to fill a session yet
signal_to_watch: Five or more Vietnamese food-protein papers a year from two or more institutions

gfi_title: Building interdisciplinary university research centers of excellence
maps_to: T5; P4; RM-04; RM-05; RM-09; ch06-knowledge-talent 6.4
vietnam_angle: Weak for a dedicated centre. Output is scattered: IUH, Nong Lam, HCMUT, HUST and others each have 2 to 6 records; GFI lists no Vietnamese research centre. Decision 1002 will recognise 50 strong research groups (30 in strategic technologies) in 2030 to 2035, which is a state route for a food-protein group
vietnam_evidence: SLW-02 (institution spread); VCO-21 re-checked 15 October 2026 (0 research centres, 0 researchers); SLW-07 (Decision 1002 strong groups and talent programmes)
verdict_note: A centre should grow round shared kit (the T5 pilot line and the P4 laboratory), not come before it. Until then a recognised strong research group under Decision 1002 is the right size
signal_to_watch: A food-protein or bioprocess group recognised as a strong research group under Decision 1002; a pilot line (RM-04) with a named academic host

gfi_title: Building alternative protein programs and majors at universities
vietnam_angle: Moderate. Food technology and bioengineering degrees are large (Can Tho University 300 and 240 places in 2026; HUST food engineering 360, snippet only). No alternative-protein major exists. MOET asks universities to build postgraduate biotechnology programmes on a 'CNSH+X' model (biotechnology plus an application field), with requested state lab investment
vietnam_evidence: INF-15 (Can Tho quotas); SLW-19 (HUST quotas, snippet, Low); SLW-08 (MOET Official Letter 5695, 17 September 2025); VCO-21 (0 courses)
verdict_note: Adds a named vehicle to RM-09: a 'biotechnology plus food process engineering' talent master's under Decision 1002, proposed through MOET's annual cycle. A full alternative-protein major is not justified: the job base is small (a wave 3 estimate puts a 10,000 t a year plant at 60 to 100 staff, Low)
signal_to_watch: A university proposes or is approved for a CNSH plus food or bioprocess talent programme; MOET's list of approved talent programmes

gfi_title: Increasing the number, quality, and diversity of alternative protein-relevant university courses
vietnam_angle: Moderate. The skills gap is specialist: extrusion, downstream processing of microbial biomass, sensory and structure of meat analogues, protein-quality scoring and food cell culture. IUH is the only Vietnamese university with recent meat-analogue papers (two in 2026). EU projects have reformed Vietnamese food curricula before (AsiFood; NutriSEA at Hue and HUST, 2015 to 2018)
vietnam_evidence: ch06 6.5 (RD-01; BIB-01); TIC-21 and SLW-18 (IUH 2026 papers); SLW-13 (NutriSEA); RD-56 (AsiFood); VCO-21 (0 courses)
verdict_note: Adds module content and a delivery route to RM-09: short specialist modules at two or three universities (IUH for texturisation, HUST for side-stream protein and fermentation, Can Tho for food technology), reusing open course material and the EU curriculum-reform model. Vietnam would adapt material, not write it from scratch
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese-language module on extrusion or downstream processing; an Erasmus+ or similar project on food protein with Vietnamese partners
source_ids: GSD-01; TIC-21; SLW-18; SLW-13; RD-56; VCO-21

gfi_title: Establishing student groups at key universities
vietnam_angle: Weak. The Alt Protein Project had 70 chapters in 21 countries in August 2024, none in Vietnam; GFI's database shows 0 Vietnamese student groups on 15 October 2026 (Thailand also 0, Malaysia 1)
verdict_note: Few employers would absorb the members. Skills for the existing fermenters and for T1 and T9 firms come first. A student group costs little and can start whenever students want one, but it is not a study recommendation
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese chapter in an Alt Protein Project cohort; T1 or T9 firms hiring graduates

gfi_title: Industry workshops, courses, and training programs
vietnam_angle: Strong need, weak supply. We found no published fermentation short course for industry: FIRI's training page lists doctoral training and one 2018 analysis course, although FIRI has fermentation and enzyme-protein departments. A food-sector short-course centre charges VND 2.4 to 4.2 million for 12 to 24 hour courses with no fermentation topic. A hands-on pilot-scale course abroad costs USD 3,100 for 21 hours
vietnam_evidence: SLW-14 and INF-01 (FIRI); SLW-16 (domestic short-course fees, Low); SLW-09 (NC State course, USD 3,100); SLW-10 (Singapore apprenticeship MOU with extrusion workshops, 2022); ECF-39 (senior process talent is the bottleneck)
verdict_note: Adds a constraint and a cost to RM-09. Fees are small; the binding input is pilot-scale kit. Hands-on fermentation training needs a pilot line, but ch28 starts RM-09 in 2027 and RM-04 only by 2030. Until then the hands-on part must run on industrial tanks of tolling hosts or abroad. A first cohort of 20 engineers on a 21-hour course of the NC State type would cost about USD 62,000 in fees, travel excluded (our calculation)
signal_to_watch: A tolling host (Vedan, Ajinomoto, Daesang) or FIRI agrees to host trainees; a regional facility (Thailand, Singapore) opens places to Vietnamese trainees
source_ids: GSD-01; SLW-09; SLW-10; SLW-14; SLW-16; INF-01; ECF-39

vietnam_angle: Moderate. Industry-funded routes are small: the Ajinomoto ASEAN+One postgraduate scholarship has supported about 16 Vietnamese students in Japan since 2009 (count ambiguous in the source). EU projects tied curricula to enterprise internships. The plays already name academic partners (VNU Hanoi fungal group for T9; FIRI for T1, T5 and T10)
vietnam_evidence: SLW-15 (Ajinomoto, press); SLW-13 (NutriSEA); plays.csv partners (T5, T9, T10)
verdict_note: Covered by RM-09 (industry placements) and the partner lists of T5, T9 and T10. GFI's researcher directory lists no Vietnamese researchers; institutions.csv already serves as the Vietnamese directory
signal_to_watch: A company-funded chair, lab or placement scheme in food fermentation at a Vietnamese university

gfi_title: Building workforce capacity through vocational programs
vietnam_angle: Moderate. Operators, not graduates, are the gap a pilot or first plant hits. A 2013 framework programme for intermediate-level fermentation technicians exists on paper (snippet only), and MOIT runs a Food Industry College in Viet Tri, but we could not confirm any college now teaching fermentation operation or its intake. RM-09 names MOET, MOST, universities and industry, not MOIT or its colleges
vietnam_evidence: SLW-20 (Circular 17/2013, snippet, Low); SLW-17 (MOIT college listing); SLW-16 (short-course centre on the college's listed domain, Low); robust_moves.csv RM-09
verdict_note: Adds lead actors and a component to RM-09: MOIT and its food colleges (and FIRI) for operator training, linked to tolling hosts. Decision 1002 does not cover this level in the summary we read (SLW-07)
signal_to_watch: A college admissions plan listing fermentation technology; an industry-college placement agreement with an amino-acid, yeast or brewing plant

scope_note: Public engagement in plant-protein making; the firm-facing core is shared trial kit
vietnam_angle: Weak for a public makerspace. The useful core for Vietnam is a shared extrusion trial line for small chay makers, which ch06 6.7 already proposes; FIRI's pilot centre covers soy milk and tofu but no extruder
vietnam_evidence: INF-02 (FIRI pilot centre); ch06 6.4 and 6.7; OQ-310 and OQ-386 (IUH extruder). GFI page text is a short description only (GSD-01)
verdict_note: A public makerspace adds little to protein security or industry. The firm-facing version, a shared extrusion trial line, is already in ch06 6.7 and the IUH extruder questions
signal_to_watch: An open food-extrusion trial service at IUH, FIRI or a hi-tech park

gfi_title: Cultivated meat makerspaces to promote public engagement
scope_note: Cultivated meat is in scope as research (T8)
vietnam_angle: None found. Vietnam has no published cultivated-meat or food cell-line work beyond one legal analysis; T8 is a research-only play
verdict_note: Biosafety, cost and the absence of a research base make a public cell-culture space premature. Any cell work belongs in T8 research partnerships
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese food cell-line project funded under T8 or RM-14

gfi_title: Alternative protein high school summer program
vietnam_evidence: No Vietnamese activity found in searches; no employer base to absorb interest
verdict_note: Too far from the study's horizon and from any Vietnamese buyer or plant. Skills for existing plants come first

vietnam_angle: Moderate. The realistic source of fermentation engineers is adjacent industry: 12 GMP-WHO veterinary vaccine plants, recombinant vaccine makers, and the amino-acid, yeast and brewing fermenters. Vietnamese-affiliated food-protein papers often carry foreign funders (Korea 11, Taiwan 10), a sign of researchers working abroad or in joint posts
vietnam_evidence: IND-34 (vaccine plants); app-s8 S8.7 adjacent talent; SLW-02 (foreign funders on Vietnam-affiliated works)
verdict_note: Adds a recruitment component to RM-09: reskill engineers from adjacent fermentation and biologics plants, and reach Vietnamese researchers abroad (OQ-056), rather than wait for new graduates
signal_to_watch: Engineers moving from vaccine or amino-acid plants into food-protein startups; returning researchers named on Vietnamese food-protein papers
